A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MultiMatch and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Existing material can be matched across relocation and renumbering, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark, class-imbalance, ablation, pseudo-label quality, and multimodal CrisisMMD results, including experiments in its appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds evaluations of SequenceMatch, CGMatch, and GPT-4o-mini, including an AG News error analysis.

M1.justification: The three-head architecture, pseudo-label weighting, losses, threshold computation, and inference procedure are retained. v3 names the threshold floor gamma_min and expands its tuning discussion; removing this floor was already tested in v1's ablation. This does not establish a new algorithmic component or changed implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five USB text datasets, their aligned and reversed class-imbalance scenarios, and two CrisisMMD tasks. The multimodal evaluation moves from v1 Appendix H to v3 Section 7. GPT-4o-mini is evaluated on existing tasks, adding no dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 6, and 7 add SequenceMatch and CGMatch to the balanced SSL comparisons. New Appendix H additionally evaluates GPT-4o-mini, substantially broadening comparison to a different model family. The imbalance and multimodal comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a separate GPT-4o-mini evaluation configuration on the retained datasets, although prompting, shot count, and decoding settings are unspecified. Existing SSL splits, training budgets, augmentation, and metrics remain unchanged. The expanded threshold-tuning discussion does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix H adds an AG News confusion matrix and qualitative analysis of GPT-4o-mini's category errors. Appendix D newly reports that removing the threshold floor works better under severe imbalance. Existing component ablations and mask-rate/impurity analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Three-run averaging, same-seed information, numerical uncertainty reporting, and the Friedman/Nemenyi framework are retained. Additional SSL rows follow existing reporting practices; the new LLM results introduce no uncertainty estimation or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds full SequenceMatch and CGMatch results, recalculated rankings, five GPT-4o-mini error rates, and its AG News confusion matrix. CGMatch achieves 6.79% error on IMDB with 100 labels versus MultiMatch's unchanged 6.98%, reducing MultiMatch's wins from nine to eight and changing its average rank from 1.10 to 1.2. Retained benchmark means, imbalance, ablation, and multimodal scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and algorithmic equations retain their substance; no theorem, proof, or formal assumption is added. Equation 6 replaces the explicit zero floor with gamma_min, still set to zero in Section 3.4, while the no-floor variant already existed in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract and results narrow the winning-setup claim from nine of ten to eight of ten while expanding the ranked comparison from 19 to 21 SSL methods. The central contribution and imbalance-robustness claims remain unchanged. The conclusion retains the outdated reference to 18 baselines.

C2.justification: New Appendix H discusses LLM comparison limitations, suggests training-data contamination from sentiment-task performance, and attributes AG News errors to semantic overlap between categories. Appendix D adds a minority-class explanation for removing the threshold floor. Existing imbalance mechanisms and general limitations are largely retained.

D1.justification: Appendix I replaces a future code-release promise with a reported public MIT-licensed USB fork containing code and experimental configurations, plus a submitted integration pull request. Appendix D adds threshold-floor tuning information and updates total compute accounting from 1,620 to 1,800 GPU hours. These materially expand reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v3 adds recent references and discussion, including VerifyMatch, SequenceMatch, CGMatch, DeCrisisMB, and further co-training/domain-adaptation work. Appendix H positions compact SSL models as complementary to LLMs. The central novelty positioning around combining existing SSL paradigms remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes targeted prose edits, expands related work, brings existing imbalance explanations into the main discussion, and moves the multimodal appendix into Section 7. It adds an LLM appendix, acknowledgements, and publication/affiliation information. Most of the existing narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1's labels are cleaned up, comparison tables gain baseline rows, and the existing multimodal table moves into the main text as Table 4. New Tables 8 and 9 display LLM errors and a confusion matrix. Existing plots and the overall two-column design are retained.

improvement.justification: The additional SSL baselines strengthen the performance comparison, including transparently reducing the claimed number of wins, while reported code/configuration access improves reproducibility. Existing multimodal evidence is easier to find. These are useful, bounded gains: the core evidence is largely unchanged, and the new LLM comparison lacks prompting details and offers a contamination interpretation unsupported by direct evidence.
